title: Signal-driven staggered canaries for pinned model revisions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: When customers pin a model revision to a route, updating that pinned revision is risky: regressions in latency, cost-per-token, or output quality can directly impact production apps. Current 'manual pin swap' flows lack a standardized, observable canary/A-B process that sits behind pins and enforces automated safety gates.

Goal: Implement a signal-driven, staggered canary rollout capability that operates behind pins and supports both canary + A/B experiments for new model revisions. The feature should enable product teams to safely surface new revisions to a tiny percentage of traffic, automatically escalate traffic based on defined quality and performance signals, and roll back on regressions. The rollout system must integrate with performance profile publishing so that each candidate revision exposes expected latency/cost baselines and model-quality eval bundles.

Core user stories:
- As a PM, I want to promote a new model revision behind an existing pin with a staged rollout rather than a big-bang swap.
- As an SRE, I want automated rollback on latency/cost regressions and alerting to avoid impacting SLAs.
- As an ML engineer, I want to run A/B experiments for output quality (eval harness) tied to live traffic slices and collect labeled signal for metric-driven decisions.
- As a platform engineer, I want the rollout to be configurable via API and viewable/controllable in Console with per-pin history and audit logs.

Constraints:
- Must work for Hosted and Dedicated deployments; Private may have opt-in telemetry requirements.
- Rollouts must respect customer-level overrides (tenants can opt out of canaries).
- Must not add A/B or canary paths that materially change end-to-end latency outside the controlled cohort.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://company.atlassian.net/l/c/rdw-canary-design (draft)
- Eval harness: github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pulls/487
- Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xx-Canary-UI
- Prototype PR (routing service): https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1642

Traceability: This ties into the pinned-model rollout spec (PM-7142) and the adaptive traffic-splitting exploration (PM-6372).
acceptance_criteria: 1) API: New /rollouts endpoint to create a 'pin-canary' resource that references an existing pin and a candidate revision. 2) Staging behavior: Initial rollout should support stages (shadow -> 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25%) where transitions can be automated or manual. 3) Signal gating: Support at least three signal classes (latency p95, error-rate 5xx, eval-quality delta on customer prompt set) with configurable thresholds. 4) Automated rollback when any signal crosses threshold for N consecutive minutes and ability to manual override. 5) Observability: Console shows per-stage metrics, historical rollouts, and links to evaluation results; audit log entries for all stage transitions. 6) No regressions in existing API contract; pins without rollouts behave unchanged. 7) End-to-end e2e tests and integration tests added to routing and telemetry pipelines. 8) Documentation: API reference, Console how-to, and recommended gating thresholds published in docs portal.
plan_steps:
1) Finalize gating signal schema and default thresholds with SRE and Applied ML. 2) Implement rollout resource and controller in routing service (ENG). 3) Add metric exporters for per-pin canary cohorts and hook into Console dashboards (Observability). 4) Wire evaluation harness to publish live-quality deltas for candidate revisions. 5) Build Console UX for creating and monitoring pin rollouts, with an escape hatch to pause/rollback. 6) Add RBAC checks and audit log entries for enterprise customers. 7) Run internal dogfood on non-critical routes for two cycles, gather telemetry and adjust thresholds. 8) Launch beta with selected customers and collect feedback, then iterate to GA.
